teile.text: In 1943 a 17‑year‑old Ingvar Kamprad launched a mail‑order business in Sweden.
teile.szene: A young man sitting at a wooden desk in Sweden in 1943 reviewing mail order letters, medium shot, warm indoor lighting.

teile.text: He named the brand after his farm, Elmtaryd, and hometown, Agunnaryd.
teile.szene: Wide exterior shot of a traditional red wooden farm in rural Smaland Sweden under a clear sky, daylight.

teile.text: Five years later he started selling furniture, turning the idea into a store.
teile.szene: A small vintage storefront in Sweden with wooden chairs displayed inside, medium shot, overcast daylight.

teile.text: IKEA grew worldwide with large stores featuring room settings and flat‑pack models.
teile.szene: A large modern furniture showroom with decorated room settings and bright overhead lighting, wide tracking shot.

teile.text: The company’s focus on cost control kept prices lower than rivals.
teile.szene: A large warehouse aisle stacked high with flat-pack furniture boxes, medium shot, clean industrial lighting.

teile.text: It has been the world’s largest furniture retailer since 2008.
teile.szene: Shoppers walking toward a large blue and yellow IKEA store entrance, exterior daylight, wide shot.

teile.text: Like, share, and save this video.
teile.szene: A customer browsing a well-lit home interior display inside a retail store, medium close up, warm lighting.

entwurf.beschreibung: Discover how a seventeen‑year‑old in Sweden founded IKEA in 1943 and built the world’s largest furniture retailer through ready‑to‑assemble designs.
